chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Jibraeel (peace be upon him) said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'Tooba (a tree in Paradise) is for the one from your community who says: There is no god except Allah, Alone, Alone, Alone.'

key_terms.طُوبَى: Tooba, a specific tree in Paradise
key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: La ilaha illa Allah, the declaration of monotheism

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting 'La ilaha illa Allah' with emphasis according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, the Angel Jibraeel conveys divine glad tidings that the Tree of Tooba in Paradise is reserved for the Prophet's community who sincerely recite the declaration of monotheism, emphasizing the power of saying 'La ilaha illa Allah' with emphasis on its oneness. Shia scholars highlight the triple repetition of 'Alone' (Wahdahu) as a profound emphasis on Tawhid al-Dhat, reflecting the purity of faith required to attain this spiritual reward. This hadith underscores the centrality of the Shahada not merely as a verbal statement but as a transformative act of devotion that secures eternal bliss.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Numan, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Jibraeelas said to Rasool-Allahsaww: ‘Tooba (a tree in the Paradise), is for the ones from yoursaww community who say, ‘There is no god except Allahazwj, Alone, Alone, Alone’’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Nu’Man from those whom he has mentioned (in his book) from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Jibril once said to the Messenger of Allah, ‘ Tuba (a tree in paradise) is for those among your followers who (sincerely) say: ‘No one deserves to be worshipped except Allah, Allah alone, Allah alone, Allah alone.’”
